passage: Many hikers believe that moss grows only on the north side of trees and can therefore be used like a compass. To test this idea, ecologist Shavkat Ergashev examined 300 trees in the Ugom forest and recorded where moss grew on each trunk. He found that moss grew wherever bark stayed damp and shaded. Near streams and on the shady floors of narrow valleys, it often covered the south, east or west sides of trunks as thickly as the north side.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Ergashev's survey showed that moss grows best on trees that stand near streams.
option_b: Hikers in the Ugom forest often get lost because they rely on moss to find their way.
option_c: Ergashev's survey showed that moss grows where bark stays damp and shaded, not reliably on the north side of trees.
option_d: Moss never grows on the north side of trees in the Ugom forest.
explanation_en:
The text sets up a belief (moss grows only on the north side) and reports Ergashev's finding that moss follows damp, shaded bark and often grows on other sides. Choice C states this main idea.

Choice A is a detail about where moss was found, not the main point. Choice B is not stated. Choice D is too extreme: moss grew on the north side too, just not only there.
explanation_uz:
Matnda avval bir qarash (mox faqat shimoliy tomonda o‘sadi) keltiriladi, so‘ng Ergashevning mox nam va soya po‘stloqda, ko‘pincha boshqa tomonlarda ham o‘sishi haqidagi natijasi beriladi. C javob asosiy g‘oyani ifodalaydi.

A asosiy fikr emas, faqat bir tafsilot. B matnda aytilmagan. D haddan tashqari: mox shimoliy tomonda ham o‘sgan, faqat u yerda emas, xolos.

passage: In the oasis town of Qumqo‘rg‘on, water from a single canal had to be shared among dozens of farming families. For centuries, the town solved this problem with a simple device. A small copper bowl with a hole in its bottom was set floating in a basin of water. Each time the bowl filled and sank, a water keeper dropped a pebble into a jar and moved the canal's flow to the next family's field. A family's share of water was measured by how many sinkings of the bowl it was allowed.
stem: According to the text, how was each family's share of canal water measured?
option_a: By the size of the field that each family farmed
option_b: By the number of times a floating bowl filled with water and sank
option_c: By the number of pebbles that each family brought to the water keeper
option_d: By the depth of the water in the canal each morning
explanation_en:
The last sentence says a family's share "was measured by how many sinkings of the bowl it was allowed." Choice B paraphrases this.

Choice A is not mentioned. Choice C misreads the pebbles: the water keeper dropped them into a jar to count sinkings. Choice D is not mentioned.
explanation_uz:
Oxirgi gapda har bir oilaning ulushi kosaning "necha marta cho‘kishi" bilan o‘lchangani aytiladi. B javob shuni o‘z so‘zlari bilan beradi.

A matnda yo‘q. C toshlarni noto‘g‘ri tushunadi: ularni suvchi cho‘kishlarni sanash uchun idishga tashlagan. D matnda yo‘q.

passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story.

Aziz gripped the handlebars so tightly that his knuckles turned white. "Don't let go," he begged, and behind him his sister Kamola promised she wouldn't. The bicycle wobbled down the lane past the bakery, past the mosque, past the old mulberry tree. Only when he reached the corner did Aziz hear Kamola's voice, far behind him, cheering. He looked back and saw her standing at the bakery, both hands in the air. He had ridden the whole way alone, and he laughed so hard he nearly fell.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Aziz is angry that his sister broke her promise to hold the bicycle.
option_b: Aziz moves from fear to joy when he discovers that he has been riding the bicycle on his own.
option_c: Kamola teaches Aziz the names of the places along the lane.
option_d: Aziz is too frightened to finish learning to ride the bicycle.
explanation_en:
Aziz begins tense and pleading, then learns that he "had ridden the whole way alone" and laughs with delight. Choice B captures this shift.

Choice A is wrong because he laughs rather than showing anger. Choice C is wrong because the places are simply what he rides past. Choice D is wrong because he rides the whole way.
explanation_uz:
Aziz avval qo‘rqib, iltimos qiladi, so‘ng butun yo‘lni "o‘zi yolg‘iz" bosib o‘tganini bilib, xursandchilikdan kuladi. B javob shu o‘zgarishni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: u jahl qilmaydi, kuladi. C noto‘g‘ri: joylar u yonidan o‘tadigan narsalar, xolos. D noto‘g‘ri: u butun yo‘lni bosib o‘tgan.

passage: In 2021, residents of the town of Bo‘ston placed a refrigerator outside the community center and invited anyone to fill it or take from it. Bakeries and grocers now leave unsold bread, fruit and vegetables there each evening, and neighbors add extra food from their gardens. Volunteers check the fridge daily and remove anything spoiled. Organizers estimate that the fridge keeps about two tons of food a year from being thrown away, while giving families who are short of money a free source of fresh food.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Bakeries in Bo‘ston have begun selling their bread at lower prices.
option_b: Volunteers in Bo‘ston must check the community fridge every day for spoiled food.
option_c: A shared community refrigerator in Bo‘ston both reduces food waste and provides free food to families in need.
option_d: Bo‘ston's community fridge has ended hunger in the town.
explanation_en:
The text describes the community fridge, how it is stocked and its two results: less food thrown away and free food for families short of money. Choice C states this.

Choice A is not mentioned. Choice B is a supporting detail, not the main idea. Choice D overstates what the text says.
explanation_uz:
Matnda jamoat muzlatkichi, uning qanday to‘ldirilishi va ikki natijasi — kamroq oziq-ovqat tashlanishi va kam ta’minlangan oilalarga bepul oziq-ovqat — tasvirlanadi. C javob shuni aytadi.

A matnda yo‘q. B asosiy g‘oya emas, yordamchi tafsilot. D matndagi fikrni bo‘rttiradi.

passage: Camels can travel for days across hot deserts without drinking, and part of their success lies in how they breathe. When a camel inhales, dry desert air passes over moist surfaces inside its long nasal passages and picks up water vapor. When the camel exhales, the warm, moist air from its lungs flows back over these surfaces, which have been cooled by the incoming air. As the exhaled air cools, much of its water vapor condenses on the surfaces and is reabsorbed instead of escaping into the air.
stem: According to the text, how do camels reduce the amount of water they lose when breathing?
option_a: They breathe much more slowly than other animals during the hottest part of the day.
option_b: They inhale moist air that adds water to their bodies.
option_c: They store extra water in their lungs before crossing deserts.
option_d: Cooled surfaces in their nasal passages cause water vapor in exhaled air to condense so that it can be reabsorbed.
explanation_en:
The text explains that exhaled air flows over cooled surfaces in the nose, where its water vapor "condenses ... and is reabsorbed." Choice D states this.

Choice A is not mentioned. Choice B is wrong because the air camels inhale is dry desert air. Choice C is not mentioned.
explanation_uz:
Matnda chiqarilayotgan havo burundagi sovigan yuzalar ustidan o‘tib, undagi suv bug‘i "kondensatsiyalanib, qayta so‘rilishi" tushuntirilgan. D javob shuni aytadi.

A matnda yo‘q. B noto‘g‘ri: tuya quruq cho‘l havosini nafasga oladi. C matnda yo‘q.

passage: In the 1920s, few adults in the mountain villages around Bog‘iston could read, and books were scarce. Teacher Saida Rahmonova found a practical solution. Each week she pasted pages of a newspaper onto the wall of the village teahouse, where men and women gathered in the evenings. Those who could read slowly sounded out the headlines for the others, and Rahmonova helped them with difficult words. Within two years, more than a hundred villagers had learned to read, many of them practicing on the very pages pinned to the teahouse wall.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: A teacher helped many adults in her village learn to read by posting newspaper pages in a public gathering place.
option_b: Newspapers in the 1920s were written in language that was too difficult for most readers.
option_c: The teahouse was the only building in the village where newspapers were allowed.
option_d: Rahmonova was the first person in the region to open a school for children.
explanation_en:
The text describes Rahmonova's method, posting newspaper pages in the teahouse, and its result: more than a hundred villagers learned to read. Choice A states this.

Choice B is not stated; Rahmonova only helped with "difficult words." Choice C is not stated. Choice D is not mentioned; the text is about adults.
explanation_uz:
Matnda Rahmonovaning usuli — choyxona devoriga gazeta sahifalarini yopishtirish — va uning natijasi: yuzdan ortiq qishloqdosh o‘qishni o‘rgangani tasvirlanadi. A javob shuni aytadi.

B aytilmagan; Rahmonova faqat "qiyin so‘zlar"da yordam bergan. C aytilmagan. D matnda yo‘q; gap kattalar haqida.

passage: Cotton farmers usually leave the soil bare between their rows of plants, which allows weeds to take hold. Agronomist Bahodir Yunusov has been testing a different approach in the Sirdaryo region: planting low-growing clover between the cotton rows. The clover shades the ground so that fewer weeds sprout. Clover is also a legume, a plant whose roots host bacteria that add nitrogen to the soil. In Yunusov's trials, fields with clover needed less weeding and less nitrogen fertilizer, while producing as much cotton as bare-soil fields.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Clover produces more valuable crops than cotton does in the Sirdaryo region.
option_b: Bacteria that live on clover roots damage cotton plants.
option_c: Growing clover between cotton rows reduced weeds and fertilizer needs without lowering cotton yields in Yunusov's trials.
option_d: Cotton farmers in the Sirdaryo region have stopped using fertilizer altogether.
explanation_en:
The text describes Yunusov's approach and its results: fewer weeds, less nitrogen fertilizer and unchanged cotton yields. Choice C states this.

Choice A is not mentioned. Choice B reverses the text: the bacteria add nitrogen, which helps. Choice D is too extreme; the fields needed "less" fertilizer, not none.
explanation_uz:
Matnda Yunusovning usuli va natijalari — kamroq begona o‘tlar, kamroq azotli o‘g‘it va o‘zgarmagan paxta hosili — tasvirlanadi. C javob shuni aytadi.

A matnda yo‘q. B matnga teskari: bakteriyalar tuproqqa azot qo‘shib, foyda beradi. D haddan tashqari: o‘g‘it "kamroq" kerak bo‘lgan, umuman kerak emas emas.

passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story.

For forty years Rahim had ferried travelers across the river, and he knew its moods as well as he knew his wife's. That morning the water looked calm enough, and the merchant on the bank was offering double the usual fare. But Rahim noticed the driftwood: whole branches, still green with leaves, turning slowly in the current. Somewhere upstream, he knew, the river had risen and torn trees from its banks, and that water was on its way. He pushed the merchant's coins back across the plank. "Tomorrow," he said.
stem: According to the text, why does Rahim refuse to cross the river?
option_a: Green branches in the water tell him that a rise in the river upstream is coming toward him.
option_b: He does not trust the merchant who wants to cross.
option_c: The fare that the merchant offers is lower than usual.
option_d: The surface of the river looks rough and dangerous.
explanation_en:
Rahim notices "whole branches, still green with leaves" and concludes that the river has risen upstream and "that water was on its way." Choice A states his reason.

Choice B is not suggested. Choice C is wrong because the merchant offers double the fare. Choice D is wrong because the water "looked calm enough."
explanation_uz:
Rahim suvda "hali yashil bargli butun shoxlar"ni ko‘radi va yuqorida daryo toshganini, o‘sha suv "yo‘lda ekanini" tushunadi. A javob uning sababini aytadi.

B matnda ishora yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: savdogar ikki barobar haq taklif qiladi. D noto‘g‘ri: suv "ancha sokin ko‘rinardi".

passage: In 2023, transportation researchers in Tashkent surveyed 1,800 commuters who had recently switched from driving to taking the metro. The most common reason they gave was reliability: 41 percent said the metro got them to work on time more consistently than driving through traffic did. Saving money came second, named by 27 percent, followed by the chance to read or rest during the trip, named by 19 percent. Concern for the environment was the main reason for only 9 percent of the commuters.
stem: According to the text, what was the most common reason the surveyed commuters gave for switching to the metro?
option_a: The metro got them to work on time more consistently.
option_b: The metro cost less than driving.
option_c: The metro let them read or rest during the trip.
option_d: The metro was better for the environment.
explanation_en:
The text says the most common reason was reliability: 41 percent said the metro got them to work on time more consistently. Choice A states this.

Choice B came second (27 percent). Choice C came third (19 percent). Choice D was the main reason for only 9 percent.
explanation_uz:
Matnga ko‘ra, eng ko‘p keltirilgan sabab ishonchlilik bo‘lgan: 41 foiz metro ishga o‘z vaqtida yetkazishini aytgan. A javob shuni bildiradi.

B ikkinchi o‘rinda (27 foiz). C uchinchi o‘rinda (19 foiz). D faqat 9 foiz uchun asosiy sabab bo‘lgan.

passage: For decades, thousands of reel-to-reel tapes from the city's old radio station sat in a damp basement, slowly decaying. The recordings included interviews, concerts and plays broadcast between 1950 and 1985. In 2019, the Navoiy Sound Museum began transferring the tapes to digital files before they became unplayable. So far, technicians have saved more than 4,000 hours of sound, and the museum has made much of it freely available online, where listeners can hear voices and music that had not been heard for half a century.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Radio programs broadcast between 1950 and 1985 were more popular than those of today.
option_b: A museum is preserving old radio recordings by converting them to digital files and sharing them with the public.
option_c: The radio station's basement was too damp to be used for storing anything.
option_d: Technicians at the museum have recorded 4,000 hours of new interviews and concerts.
explanation_en:
The text describes decaying tapes, the museum's project to digitize them and the results: more than 4,000 hours saved and shared online. Choice B states this main idea.

Choice A is not discussed. Choice C is a minor detail, and it overstates the text. Choice D is wrong because the 4,000 hours were saved from old tapes, not newly recorded.
explanation_uz:
Matnda yemirilayotgan lentalar, muzeyning ularni raqamlashtirish loyihasi va natijalari — 4 000 soatdan ortiq ovoz saqlanib, internetda ochiq qo‘yilgani — tasvirlanadi. B javob asosiy g‘oyani beradi.

A muhokama qilinmagan. C kichik tafsilot va u ham bo‘rttirilgan. D noto‘g‘ri: 4 000 soat yangi yozilmagan, eski lentalardan saqlab qolingan.

passage: Volcanologists monitor the gases that rise from a volcano's crater, because a sudden change in the mix of gases can warn that an eruption is approaching. Collecting samples, however, is risky: the gases are often toxic, and the crater rim can collapse without warning. At the Qizilsoy volcano, a team led by Laziz Abdurahimov now uses small drones fitted with gas sensors. The drones fly directly through the plume above the crater and send readings back to scientists standing safely several kilometers away.
stem: According to the text, why does Abdurahimov's team use drones at the Qizilsoy volcano?
option_a: The drones can stop toxic gases from escaping from the crater.
option_b: The drones can predict the exact day on which an eruption will begin.
option_c: The drones are less expensive than the sensors that scientists usually use.
option_d: The drones allow the team to measure crater gases without exposing people to dangerous conditions.
explanation_en:
The text says collecting gas samples is risky because the gases are toxic and the crater rim can collapse, so drones fly through the plume while scientists stay "safely several kilometers away." Choice D states this.

Choice A is wrong because the drones only measure the gases. Choice B overstates the text: gas changes "can warn" of an eruption. Choice C is not mentioned.
explanation_uz:
Matnga ko‘ra, gaz namunalarini olish xavfli: gazlar zaharli, krater cheti esa to‘satdan qulashi mumkin. Shuning uchun dronlar tutun ichidan uchadi, olimlar esa "bir necha kilometr narida xavfsiz" turadi. D javob shuni aytadi.

A noto‘g‘ri: dronlar faqat gazlarni o‘lchaydi. B matnni bo‘rttiradi: gaz o‘zgarishi faqat "ogohlantirishi mumkin". C matnda yo‘q.

passage: The stone bridge over the Ko‘ksuv River, built in the sixteenth century, has survived floods that destroyed many newer bridges nearby. Engineers who studied it in 2020 found an explanation in its design. Above each of its piers, the builders left a small arched opening through the bridge itself. When floodwater rises higher than the main arches, it can pass through these openings instead of pushing against a solid wall of stone. The openings greatly reduce the force the water exerts on the bridge.
stem: According to the text, what helps the bridge survive floods?
option_a: Its piers were built from a harder stone than those of newer bridges.
option_b: Its main arches are higher than any flood the river has ever produced.
option_c: Engineers strengthened it with new materials in 2020.
option_d: Openings above its piers let high floodwater pass through the bridge.
explanation_en:
The engineers found that small openings above the piers let rising floodwater pass through "instead of pushing against a solid wall of stone," reducing the force on the bridge. Choice D states this.

Choice A is not mentioned. Choice B is wrong because the text describes floods rising "higher than the main arches." Choice C is wrong because the engineers studied the bridge; they did not repair it.
explanation_uz:
Muhandislar ustunlar ustidagi kichik ochiqliklar ko‘tarilgan suvni "yaxlit tosh devorga urilish o‘rniga" o‘tkazib yuborishini aniqlagan; bu ko‘prikka ta’sir etuvchi kuchni kamaytiradi. D javob shuni aytadi.

A matnda yo‘q. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda toshqin "asosiy ravoqlardan baland" ko‘tarilishi aytiladi. C noto‘g‘ri: muhandislar ko‘prikni o‘rganishgan, ta’mirlashmagan.

passage: Gardeners often welcome earthworms as a sign of healthy soil. In many forests of northern North America, however, earthworms are newcomers. Glaciers scraped the region bare thousands of years ago, and most native earthworms never returned; the species found there today arrived largely with European settlers. In a study of maple forests in that region, ecologist Nilufar Qosimova found that where earthworms had spread, the thick layer of fallen leaves on the forest floor had almost vanished, and several wildflowers that depend on that layer had become rare.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Earthworms improve the soil in every forest they reach.
option_b: Earthworms, though often seen as beneficial, can harm forests in regions where they are not native.
option_c: Glaciers destroyed most of the wildflowers in northern North America.
option_d: European settlers brought earthworms to North America in order to improve its forests.
explanation_en:
The text contrasts the usual view of earthworms as healthy for soil with Qosimova's finding that, in northern forests where they are newcomers, they removed the leaf layer and made some wildflowers rare. Choice B states this.

Choice A contradicts the study. Choice C is wrong because the text links the wildflowers' decline to earthworms, not glaciers. Choice D adds a purpose the text never states.
explanation_uz:
Matnda yomg‘ir chuvalchanglari tuproq uchun foydali degan odatiy qarash Qosimovaning natijasiga qarama-qarshi qo‘yiladi: ular yangi kelgan shimoliy o‘rmonlarda barg qatlamini yo‘qotib, ayrim yovvoyi gullarni kamaytirgan. B javob shuni aytadi.

A tadqiqotga zid. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda gullar kamayishi muzliklarga emas, chuvalchanglarga bog‘langan. D matnda aytilmagan maqsadni qo‘shadi.

passage: Historians have usually assumed that the guides who led caravans across the deserts of Central Asia carried their knowledge only in memory, passing it on by word of mouth. That picture is changing. In a private library in Xiva, historian Jasur Ibrohimov has identified four small notebooks kept by nineteenth-century caravan guides. The notebooks record the distances between wells, which wells turned salty in late summer and which passes were blocked by snow in particular months, all written in a compact shorthand the guides seem to have shared.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Newly identified notebooks show that some caravan guides recorded their route knowledge in writing, not only in memory.
option_b: Caravan guides in the nineteenth century could not read or write.
option_c: Many wells along the caravan routes turned salty in late summer.
option_d: Caravan guides refused to share their knowledge with anyone outside their families.
explanation_en:
The text presents an older assumption (guides kept knowledge only in memory) and then evidence that changes it: notebooks in which guides wrote down detailed route information. Choice A states this.

Choice B contradicts the notebooks. Choice C is one detail recorded in the notebooks, not the main idea. Choice D is not supported; the shorthand seems to have been shared among guides.
explanation_uz:
Matnda eski taxmin (karvonboshilar bilimni faqat xotirada saqlagan) va uni o‘zgartiruvchi dalil — yo‘l ma’lumotlari yozilgan daftarlar — keltiriladi. A javob shuni aytadi.

B daftarlarga zid. C daftarlardagi bitta tafsilot, asosiy g‘oya emas. D asossiz: qisqa yozuv karvonboshilar orasida umumiy bo‘lgan ko‘rinadi.

passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Timur, a cellist, has returned to the concert hall where he performed for thirty years.

The hall was empty, the seats covered in gray cloth, and Timur's footsteps echoed as if someone were following him. He had expected to feel sad here. Instead, standing at the edge of the stage, he found himself listening. The building creaked and ticked as it cooled in the evening air, and the sound rose into the high ceiling exactly as his cello once had. He smiled. The hall, it seemed, had not stopped making music just because he had.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Timur is overwhelmed by grief at the sight of the empty concert hall.
option_b: Timur decides to return to performing in the concert hall.
option_c: Returning to the hall, Timur finds an unexpected comfort in the sounds the empty building still makes.
option_d: Timur is frightened by footsteps that seem to follow him through the hall.
explanation_en:
Timur "expected to feel sad" but instead listens to the hall's creaks and smiles, thinking the hall "had not stopped making music." Choice C captures this.

Choice A is wrong because the text says he does not feel the sadness he expected. Choice B is not stated. Choice D misreads a comparison: the echo only sounds "as if" someone were following him.
explanation_uz:
Timur "g‘amgin bo‘laman deb kutgan", lekin aksincha zalning g‘ichirlashiga quloq solib, jilmayadi va zal "musiqa chalishdan to‘xtamagan" deb o‘ylaydi. C javob shuni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda u kutgan g‘amni his qilmagani aytiladi. B aytilmagan. D o‘xshatishni noto‘g‘ri tushunadi: aks-sado faqat "go‘yo" kimdir ergashayotgandek eshitiladi.

passage: Hoping to encourage healthier eating, a university in Samarkand moved the fruit in its cafeterias from a back shelf to a basket beside the cash registers. Economist Shahzoda Murodova tracked purchases for a semester before and after the change. Fruit sales nearly doubled. However, the total number of calories that students bought per meal did not change: many students simply added a piece of fruit to the meals they would have bought anyway, rather than replacing other foods with it.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Moving fruit to the cash registers made students' meals much healthier.
option_b: Moving fruit to the cash registers led students to buy much more fruit, but not to buy fewer calories overall.
option_c: Students at the university bought less fruit after it was moved beside the cash registers.
option_d: Students at the university chose fruit instead of other foods once it was easy to reach.
explanation_en:
The text reports two results of the change: fruit sales nearly doubled, but total calories per meal stayed the same because students added fruit rather than substituting it. Choice B states both.

Choice A overstates the result, ignoring the unchanged calories. Choice C contradicts the doubling of sales. Choice D contradicts the text, which says students added fruit "rather than replacing other foods with it."
explanation_uz:
Matnda o‘zgarishning ikki natijasi beriladi: meva savdosi deyarli ikki barobar oshgan, lekin talabalar mevani boshqa taom o‘rniga emas, qo‘shimcha olgani uchun umumiy kaloriya o‘zgarmagan. B javob ikkalasini ham aytadi.

A natijani bo‘rttiradi, o‘zgarmagan kaloriyani e’tiborsiz qoldiradi. C savdo ikki barobar oshganiga zid. D matnga zid: talabalar mevani "boshqa taomlar o‘rniga emas", qo‘shimcha olgan.

passage: Spider silk is famous for its strength, but biologist Dilshoda Rasulova wondered how humidity affects it. She collected silk from orb-weaving spiders and stretched single threads until they broke, first in dry air and then in air that was nearly saturated with water. In humid air, the threads stretched to almost twice their dry length before breaking, but they broke under slightly less force. Rasulova suggests that the extra stretch may help webs absorb the impact of insects striking them on damp mornings.
stem: According to the text, what did Rasulova observe about spider silk in humid air?
option_a: It broke under much more force than silk in dry air.
option_b: It became too weak to hold insects that struck the web.
option_c: It stretched less than silk in dry air but became far stronger.
option_d: It stretched much further before breaking, though it broke under slightly less force than in dry air.
explanation_en:
The text says that in humid air threads "stretched to almost twice their dry length" but broke "under slightly less force." Choice D states both observations.

Choice A reverses the force result. Choice B is not supported; Rasulova suggests the extra stretch may help webs absorb insect impacts. Choice C reverses both results.
explanation_uz:
Matnga ko‘ra, nam havoda iplar "quruq holatdagidan deyarli ikki barobar" cho‘zilgan, lekin "biroz kamroq kuch" bilan uzilgan. D javob ikkala kuzatuvni ham beradi.

A kuch natijasini teskari qiladi. B asossiz: Rasulova aksincha, qo‘shimcha cho‘ziluvchanlik to‘rga hasharot zarbasini yutishga yordam berishi mumkin deydi. C ikkala natijani ham teskari qiladi.

passage: The composer Vali Shukurov (1902–1967) revised his Second Symphony seven times over twenty years, and scholars have often attributed these revisions to perfectionism. Musicologist Lola Ahmedova offers a more specific explanation. Studying the margins of Shukurov's scores, she found notes copied from conversations with orchestra players: a horn player's complaint that one passage left no time to breathe, a violinist's warning that a run of notes was nearly impossible at the written speed. Nearly every revision, Ahmedova found, changed a passage the players had complained about.
stem: According to the text, what did Ahmedova find about Shukurov's revisions to his Second Symphony?
option_a: They made the symphony longer and more difficult to perform.
option_b: They were made mainly because critics disliked the first performance.
option_c: Most of them changed passages that orchestra players had described as difficult to perform.
option_d: They were all made within a single year.
explanation_en:
Ahmedova found players' complaints copied into the scores and that "nearly every revision" changed a passage the players had complained about. Choice C states this finding.

Choice A is not stated and conflicts with revisions that answered players' difficulties. Choice B is wrong because critics are not mentioned. Choice D contradicts the twenty-year span.
explanation_uz:
Ahmedova partituralar hoshiyasida musiqachilarning shikoyatlari yozib qo‘yilganini va "deyarli har bir tahrir" ular shikoyat qilgan joyni o‘zgartirganini aniqlagan. C javob shu natijani beradi.

A aytilmagan va musiqachilarning qiyinchiliklarini hal qilgan tahrirlarga zid. B noto‘g‘ri: tanqidchilar tilga olinmagan. D yigirma yillik muddatga zid.

passage: Fallen leaves and dead wood are broken down mainly by fungi, which return the nutrients they contain to the soil. To learn how drought affects this process, ecologist Kamron Sattorov covered plots of a pistachio woodland with clear roofs that blocked half of the rain for three years. Under the roofs, fungi grew more sparsely, and leaves that would normally have decayed within two years were still largely intact. Sattorov warns that if droughts become more frequent, nutrients could remain locked in dead plant material for longer, leaving less available for new growth.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Fungi in the pistachio woodland grew faster when rainfall was reduced.
option_b: Pistachio trees need less rain than most other trees to survive.
option_c: Clear roofs are the best way to protect woodlands from drought.
option_d: Reducing rainfall slowed the breakdown of dead plant material by fungi, which could limit the nutrients available to plants.
explanation_en:
Sattorov's experiment showed that with less rain, fungi grew sparsely and leaves stayed intact, and he warns that more droughts could leave fewer nutrients for new growth. Choice D states this.

Choice A reverses the finding. Choice B is not discussed. Choice C misunderstands the roofs, which were used to *create* drought conditions.
explanation_uz:
Sattorov tajribasi yomg‘ir kamayganda zamburug‘lar siyrak o‘sib, barglar chirimay qolganini ko‘rsatgan; u qurg‘oqchilik ko‘payasa, yangi o‘sish uchun ozuqa kamayishi mumkinligidan ogohlantiradi. D javob shuni aytadi.

A natijani teskari qiladi. B muhokama qilinmagan. C tomlarni noto‘g‘ri tushunadi: ular qurg‘oqchilikni *yaratish* uchun ishlatilgan.

passage:
The following text is from a poem. The speaker is waiting at a small railway station late at night.

The last train is an hour late, and still
the stationmaster sweeps the empty platform
as carefully as if a king were coming.
Above him, one lamp hums and gathers moths,
a small bright town that no one else will visit.
I watch him sweep, and wait, and do not mind.
stem: Based on the text, how does the speaker respond to the train's delay?
option_a: The speaker grows angry at the stationmaster for the delay.
option_b: The speaker waits calmly, watching the scene at the station without complaint.
option_c: The speaker leaves the station to look for another way home.
option_d: The speaker helps the stationmaster sweep the platform.
explanation_en:
The last line says the speaker watches, waits "and do[es] not mind." The speaker observes the stationmaster and the lamp calmly. Choice B states this.

Choice A is wrong because the speaker does not blame anyone. Choice C is wrong because the speaker keeps waiting. Choice D is wrong because the speaker only watches the stationmaster sweep.
explanation_uz:
Oxirgi qatorda so‘zlovchi kuzatib, kutib turishi va "bunga qarshi emasligi" aytiladi. U stansiya boshlig‘i va chiroqni xotirjam kuzatadi. B javob shuni bildiradi.

A noto‘g‘ri: so‘zlovchi hech kimni ayblamaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: u kutishda davom etadi. D noto‘g‘ri: u faqat stansiya boshlig‘ining supurishini kuzatadi.

passage: Language-learning apps have become popular among adults in Uzbekistan who want to learn English. Education researcher Otabek Nurmatov compared 200 adults who studied with an app for six months with 200 who attended weekly community classes. On vocabulary tests, the app users did as well as the class members. But when the two groups were asked to hold a ten-minute conversation, the class members spoke far more fluently. Nurmatov concludes that apps can teach words effectively but offer too little practice in actually speaking.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Nurmatov's study found that language apps are more effective than classes in every respect.
option_b: Nurmatov's study found that adults who attend classes learn more vocabulary than app users.
option_c: Language-learning apps are more popular than community classes in Uzbekistan.
option_d: Nurmatov's study found that language apps taught vocabulary as well as classes did but were less effective at building speaking skills.
explanation_en:
The study shows equal vocabulary results but much better conversation among class members, and Nurmatov concludes that apps teach words but give too little speaking practice. Choice D states this.

Choice A contradicts the conversation results. Choice B is wrong because vocabulary results were equal. Choice C is not stated; the text says only that apps "have become popular."
explanation_uz:
Tadqiqotda lug‘at natijalari teng, suhbatda esa kursdagilar ancha ravon gapirgani aniqlangan; Nurmatov ilovalar so‘z o‘rgatadi, lekin gapirish amaliyoti kam degan xulosaga keladi. D javob shuni aytadi.

A suhbat natijalariga zid. B noto‘g‘ri: lug‘at natijalari teng bo‘lgan. C aytilmagan; matnda faqat ilovalar "ommalashgani" aytilgan.

passage: In the 1840s, the mapmaker Qurbon Mirzo produced a set of hand-drawn maps of the Ustyurt plateau for the khan of Xiva. Earlier maps of the plateau showed mainly towns and rivers, of which the region had few. Qurbon Mirzo's maps instead marked every well, along with notes on how deep each was, whether its water was sweet or bitter and how many camels it could serve in a day. Travelers' accounts from the period suggest that copies of these maps were valued above almost any other possession by merchants crossing the plateau.
stem: According to the text, how did Qurbon Mirzo's maps differ from earlier maps of the Ustyurt plateau?
option_a: They showed many more towns and rivers than earlier maps did.
option_b: They were the first maps of the plateau to be drawn by hand.
option_c: They recorded detailed information about the region's wells.
option_d: They were made for merchants rather than for a ruler.
explanation_en:
Earlier maps showed "mainly towns and rivers," but Qurbon Mirzo's maps "instead marked every well" with notes on depth, water quality and capacity. Choice C states this difference.

Choice A is wrong because the region had few towns and rivers, and the new maps focused on wells. Choice B is not stated. Choice D is wrong because the maps were made for the khan.
explanation_uz:
Avvalgi xaritalarda "asosan shaharlar va daryolar" ko‘rsatilgan, Qurbon Mirzo esa "har bir quduqni" chuqurligi, suv sifati va sig‘imi bilan belgilagan. C javob shu farqni aytadi.

A noto‘g‘ri: hududda shahar va daryo kam bo‘lgan, yangi xaritalar quduqlarga qaratilgan. B aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: xaritalar xon uchun tayyorlangan.

passage: Ice cores, long cylinders drilled from glaciers, contain air bubbles and dust that record past climates. Glaciologist Feruza Halimova has found that the cores she drilled from a glacier in the Pamir Mountains hold another kind of record: pollen. Wind carries pollen grains from surrounding valleys onto the glacier, where they are buried in the yearly layers of snow. By identifying pollen from layers thousands of years old, Halimova has shown that walnut forests once grew in valleys that are now covered only by grass and shrubs.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Pollen preserved in glacier ice has allowed Halimova to reconstruct what plants grew in nearby valleys long ago.
option_b: Air bubbles in ice cores are the most reliable record of past climates.
option_c: Walnut forests in the Pamir valleys were destroyed by advancing glaciers.
option_d: Pollen grains can travel only a short distance before they fall to the ground.
explanation_en:
The text introduces pollen as a new kind of record in ice cores and shows how Halimova used it to learn that walnut forests once grew in now-grassy valleys. Choice A states this.

Choice B is not claimed; the text does not rank records. Choice C gives a cause that the text never mentions. Choice D is not supported; wind carries pollen from surrounding valleys onto the glacier.
explanation_uz:
Matnda gulchang muz namunalaridagi yangi turdagi yozuv sifatida tanishtiriladi va Halimova u orqali hozir o‘tloq bo‘lgan vodiylarda qachonlardir yong‘oqzorlar bo‘lganini aniqlagani ko‘rsatiladi. A javob shuni aytadi.

B da’vo qilinmagan; matn yozuvlarni solishtirmaydi. C matnda tilga olinmagan sababni keltiradi. D asossiz: shamol gulchangni atrofdagi vodiylardan muzlikka olib keladi.

passage: The medieval epic *Gul and Navro‘z* has been translated into English three times, and each translation reflects a different idea of what a translator owes the original. The first, from 1911, turned the poem into rhyming English verse, changing many images to make the rhymes work. The second, from 1964, gave up rhyme entirely to follow the original's meaning line by line. The most recent, by Nodira Usmonova, keeps the line-by-line meaning but adds internal echoes of sound to suggest the music of the original without forcing rhymes.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Three English translations of the same epic reflect different choices about how to balance the original's sound and meaning.
option_b: The 1911 translation of the epic is the most accurate of the three.
option_c: Usmonova's translation is the first to follow the original line by line.
option_d: Medieval epics are impossible to translate into English.
explanation_en:
The text describes three translations and how each handles the trade-off between sound (rhyme, echoes) and meaning (line-by-line accuracy). Choice A states this.

Choice B is wrong because the 1911 version changed many images. Choice C is wrong because the 1964 version already did this. Choice D is too extreme and not claimed.
explanation_uz:
Matnda uchta tarjima va ularning har biri ohang (qofiya, tovush uyg‘unligi) bilan ma’no (satrma-satr aniqlik) o‘rtasidagi muvozanatni qanday hal qilgani tasvirlanadi. A javob shuni aytadi.

B noto‘g‘ri: 1911-yilgi tarjimada ko‘p obrazlar o‘zgartirilgan. C noto‘g‘ri: buni 1964-yilgi tarjima allaqachon qilgan. D haddan tashqari va matnda aytilmagan.

passage: To control rodents that damage crops, farmers in the Qashqadaryo region have mounted hundreds of nest boxes for barn owls on poles across their fields. Biologist Sanjar Rahmatullayev found that owls occupied most of the boxes and that each owl family caught thousands of rodents a year. Yet surveys showed no drop in the overall rodent population across the region, which recovered quickly through rapid breeding. Crop damage did fall, however, within about a kilometer of occupied boxes, where the owls did most of their hunting.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Although nest boxes did not reduce the region's rodent population as a whole, they did lower crop damage near the boxes.
option_b: Nest boxes for barn owls failed to provide any benefit to farmers in the Qashqadaryo region.
option_c: Barn owls in the Qashqadaryo region caught enough rodents to sharply reduce the regional rodent population.
option_d: Barn owls in the Qashqadaryo region rarely used the nest boxes that farmers provided.
explanation_en:
The text gives a mixed result: the owls caught many rodents, but the regional rodent population did not drop; crop damage still fell near occupied boxes. Choice A captures both parts.

Choice B ignores the reduced crop damage. Choice C contradicts the surveys showing no regional drop. Choice D contradicts the finding that owls occupied most boxes.
explanation_uz:
Matnda aralash natija beriladi: boyqushlar ko‘p kemiruvchini tutgan, ammo hududdagi kemiruvchilar soni kamaymagan; shunga qaramay, band uyalar yaqinida hosilga zarar kamaygan. A javob ikkala qismni ham qamrab oladi.

B hosil zarari kamayganini e’tiborsiz qoldiradi. C hududda kamayish bo‘lmaganini ko‘rsatgan kuzatuvlarga zid. D boyqushlar uyalarning ko‘pchiligini egallaganiga zid.

passage: A chronicle written in the town of Kesh describes a terrible famine in the years 1426–1428, claiming that drought "left the fields as bare as a threshing floor" and that two of every three townspeople died. Historians have generally dismissed the account as exaggerated. Tree-ring evidence gathered by climatologist Ozoda Fozilova now shows that 1426–1428 were the driest three consecutive years in the region in five centuries. Fozilova cautions, though, that tree rings record rainfall, not deaths, and that the chronicle's death toll still lacks any independent support.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: New climate evidence proves that the chronicle's account of the famine is accurate in every detail.
option_b: Historians were right to dismiss the chronicle's account of a drought as exaggerated.
option_c: New climate evidence supports the chronicle's report of a severe drought, but not its claim about how many people died.
option_d: Tree-ring evidence shows that the famine killed fewer people than the chronicle claims.
explanation_en:
Fozilova's tree rings confirm an extreme drought in 1426–1428, supporting part of the chronicle, but she notes that tree rings cannot confirm the death toll. Choice C states this divided conclusion.

Choice A is too extreme, since the death toll is unsupported. Choice B contradicts the confirmation of the drought. Choice D is wrong because tree rings say nothing about deaths, so they cannot show the toll was lower.
explanation_uz:
Fozilovaning daraxt halqalari 1426–1428-yillardagi o‘ta kuchli qurg‘oqchilikni tasdiqlaydi — bu solnomaning bir qismini qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi; ammo u daraxt halqalari o‘limlar sonini tasdiqlay olmasligini ta’kidlaydi. C javob shu ikki qismli xulosani beradi.

A haddan tashqari: o‘lim soni tasdiqlanmagan. B qurg‘oqchilik tasdiqlanganiga zid. D noto‘g‘ri: daraxt halqalari o‘lim haqida hech narsa demaydi, demak sonni kamroq deb ham ko‘rsata olmaydi.

passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Malika is preparing to tell her father that she has left medical school to study painting.

It made no difference to her, Malika told herself, what her father thought. She was twenty-three; the decision was made. On the bus to his house she went over it once more: first the good grades from her first year, so he would know she had not failed; then the gallery that had bought two of her paintings; then, if his face darkened, the teacher who had called her talent rare. She had written the order on the back of a ticket, and she read it again as the bus turned onto his street.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Malika has decided to return to medical school to please her father.
option_b: Malika is confident that her father will approve of her decision.
option_c: Malika has not yet decided whether to leave medical school.
option_d: Malika insists that her father's opinion does not matter to her, yet her careful preparation suggests that it matters a great deal.
explanation_en:
Malika tells herself her father's opinion makes "no difference," but she rehearses a careful sequence of arguments, written down and reread, to win his approval. The contrast reveals that his opinion matters to her, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because "the decision was made" to study painting. Choice B is wrong because she prepares for his face to darken. Choice C contradicts "the decision was made."
explanation_uz:
Malika o‘ziga otasining fikri "farqi yo‘q" deydi, lekin uning roziligini olish uchun dalillarni puxta tartib bilan tayyorlaydi, chiptaga yozib, qayta o‘qiydi. Bu qarama-qarshilik otasining fikri unga juda muhim ekanini ko‘rsatadi — D javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: rassomlikni o‘qish haqida "qaror qabul qilingan". B noto‘g‘ri: u otasining qovog‘i solinishiga tayyorlanadi. C "qaror qabul qilingan" degan gapga zid.

passage: Small loans to people who want to start businesses have been promoted as a way out of poverty. Economist Rustam Qobilov studied 1,500 households in Namangan province, half of which were offered such loans. Over three years, households offered loans opened more new businesses than the others, but their average incomes rose no faster. Most of the new businesses earned little. The gains were concentrated among a small group of households that already ran established shops before the loans arrived; for them, the loans led to much larger profits.
stem: According to the text, what did Qobilov find about the households that were offered loans?
option_a: They started more businesses, and their average incomes rose much faster than those of other households.
option_b: They started more businesses, but their incomes rose faster only among households that already ran shops.
option_c: They started no more businesses than other households did, but their incomes rose faster.
option_d: They used the loans mainly to pay for household needs rather than to start businesses.
explanation_en:
Qobilov found more new businesses but no faster rise in average income; the gains went mostly to households that already had established shops. Choice B states this.

Choice A contradicts the finding that average incomes "rose no faster." Choice C reverses both results. Choice D is not supported; the households did open more businesses.
explanation_uz:
Qobilov kredit taklif qilinganlar ko‘proq biznes ochganini, lekin o‘rtacha daromad tezroq o‘smaganini aniqlagan; foyda asosan avvaldan do‘koni bor xonadonlarga tushgan. B javob shuni aytadi.

A o‘rtacha daromad "tezroq o‘smagan" degan natijaga zid. C ikkala natijani ham teskari qiladi. D asossiz: xonadonlar haqiqatan ham ko‘proq biznes ochgan.

passage: On cold nights, hummingbirds can enter torpor, a deep, sleep-like state in which their body temperature and heart rate drop sharply, saving energy that would otherwise be spent keeping warm. Biologist Shirin Abduvaliyeva expected the birds she studied to use torpor only on the coldest nights. Instead, she found that in the weeks before their autumn migration, the birds entered torpor even on mild nights, while they were steadily gaining weight. Abduvaliyeva suggests that by saving energy at night, the birds could store more fat for the long journey ahead.
stem: According to the text, what was unexpected about the hummingbirds Abduvaliyeva studied?
option_a: They entered torpor on the coldest nights of the year.
option_b: They lost weight in the weeks before their autumn migration.
option_c: Before migrating, they entered torpor even on nights that were not especially cold.
option_d: Their body temperature rose sharply when they entered torpor.
explanation_en:
Abduvaliyeva "expected" torpor only on the coldest nights but found that, before migration, the birds used it "even on mild nights." Choice C states what was unexpected.

Choice A is what she expected, not the surprise. Choice B is wrong because the birds were "steadily gaining weight." Choice D reverses the text: body temperature drops in torpor.
explanation_uz:
Abduvaliyeva torpor faqat eng sovuq kechalarda bo‘ladi deb "kutgan", lekin migratsiyadan oldin qushlar uni "hatto iliq kechalarda ham" qo‘llaganini aniqlagan. C javob kutilmagan holatni aytadi.

A u kutgan narsa, kutilmagan emas. B noto‘g‘ri: qushlar "muntazam vazn olgan". D matnga teskari: torporda tana harorati pasayadi.

passage: Critics of the recent revival of suzani embroidery in Bukhara often complain that it is not authentic. Traditional suzanis were sewn for a bride's dowry and hung in the family home; today's are mostly sold to tourists and hotels. Yet art historian Sabina Haydarova argues that this criticism misses what has survived. The stitches, the natural dyes and the patterns passed from mother to daughter remain largely as they were a century ago. What has changed, she argues, is only the purpose the cloth serves, and crafts have always adapted their purposes in order to survive.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Haydarova argues that suzanis made for tourists are lower in quality than traditional suzanis.
option_b: Haydarova argues that the suzani revival keeps traditional methods alive while serving new purposes, a change she sees as no reason to call it inauthentic.
option_c: Haydarova agrees with critics that the revival has abandoned traditional embroidery techniques.
option_d: Haydarova argues that suzanis should once again be sewn only for brides' dowries.
explanation_en:
The text presents critics' charge of inauthenticity and Haydarova's reply: the techniques survive, only the purpose has changed, and crafts have always adapted their purposes to survive. Choice B states her argument.

Choice A is not stated. Choice C reverses her view that stitches, dyes and patterns "remain largely as they were." Choice D contradicts her acceptance of new purposes.
explanation_uz:
Matnda tanqidchilarning "haqiqiy emas" degan da’vosi va Haydarovaning javobi beriladi: usullar saqlanib qolgan, faqat maqsad o‘zgargan, hunarmandchilik esa omon qolish uchun doim maqsadini moslashtirgan. B javob uning fikrini ifodalaydi.

A aytilmagan. C uning choklar, bo‘yoqlar va naqshlar "deyarli o‘zgarmagan" degan fikriga teskari. D uning yangi maqsadlarni qabul qilishiga zid.

passage: Microplastics, tiny fragments of plastic, are increasingly found in farm soils, and many studies have reported that they harm soil animals. Soil biologist Akbar Zokirov suspected that such general claims hide important differences. He mixed equal amounts of two kinds of microplastic into soil containing earthworms: thin fibers shed from synthetic clothing, and small irregular fragments from broken packaging. After two months, worms in soil with fibers had dug about 40 percent fewer burrows than worms in clean soil, while worms in soil with fragments burrowed about as much as those in clean soil.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Zokirov's experiment suggests that the effect of microplastics on earthworms depends on the type of plastic involved.
option_b: Zokirov's experiment shows that microplastics do not harm earthworms.
option_c: Zokirov's experiment shows that all microplastics reduce earthworm burrowing by about 40 percent.
option_d: Zokirov's experiment shows that microplastics from packaging are more harmful than fibers from clothing.
explanation_en:
Zokirov suspected that general claims hide differences, and his results show exactly that: fibers reduced burrowing by about 40 percent, while fragments had no such effect. Choice A states this main idea.

Choice B ignores the harm from fibers. Choice C overgeneralizes the fiber result to all microplastics. Choice D reverses which type caused harm.
explanation_uz:
Zokirov umumiy da’volar muhim farqlarni yashiradi deb gumon qilgan va natijalari buni ko‘rsatgan: tolalar inlar sonini taxminan 40 foizga kamaytirgan, bo‘laklar esa bunday ta’sir qilmagan. A javob asosiy g‘oyani beradi.

B tolalarning zararini e’tiborsiz qoldiradi. C tola natijasini barcha mikroplastiklarga umumlashtiradi. D qaysi tur zarar berganini teskari qiladi.

passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Ergash, an elderly mapmaker, is looking at a map he drew fifty years earlier.

The river was in the wrong place. Ergash saw it at once: he had drawn it a full finger's width east of where it ran, and the village of Sarmich, which he had never visited, sat proudly on the wrong bank. A younger man would have been ashamed. Ergash found that he was smiling. He remembered the summer he had drawn it, the borrowed tent, the guide who had sworn the river turned east, his own certainty. The mistakes were the only part of the map that still looked like him.
stem: Which choice best describes Ergash's response to the errors in his old map?
option_a: He is ashamed of them and wishes he could correct the map.
option_b: He blames the guide for every mistake that appears on the map.
option_c: He is surprised to learn that the village of Sarmich exists.
option_d: He regards them with affection because they recall who he was when he made the map.
explanation_en:
Ergash notes that "a younger man would have been ashamed" but finds himself smiling as the errors bring back memories; they are "the only part of the map that still looked like him." Choice D captures this fondness.

Choice A is what a younger man might feel, not Ergash. Choice B is too strong: he remembers the guide's claim but also "his own certainty," and he blames no one. Choice C is not supported; he knew of the village but had never visited it.
explanation_uz:
Ergash "yoshroq odam uyalgan bo‘lardi" deydi, lekin xatolar xotiralarni uyg‘otgani uchun jilmayadi; ular "xaritaning hali ham unga o‘xshaydigan yagona qismi". D javob shu mehrni ifodalaydi.

A — yoshroq odamning tuyg‘usi, Ergashniki emas. B haddan tashqari: u yo‘lboshlovchining gapini ham, "o‘z ishonchini" ham eslaydi, hech kimni ayblamaydi. C asossiz: u qishloqni bilgan, faqat u yerda bo‘lmagan.
